text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-French President Chirac will meet Prime Minister Hariri in Paris on January 4 to discuss the results of the "Friends of Lebanon" conference which was held in Washington on Dec 16.
-Eleven people remain in custody following the wide campaign of arrests launched by security forces in the last ten days, official sources said.
-The five-nation committee monitoring a ceasefire in Lebanon will meet on January 5 to discuss two Israeli and one Lebanese complaint for recent violations of the ceasefire in south Lebanon.
-Lebanon's trade balance suffers a deficit and the cost of services is high, the Banks Association stated in its annual report.
-PM Hariri said the arrest campaign was done in accordance to the judicial procedures.
-The commercial banks lend the private sector $2935 million and the public sector $2275 million in 1996, the Banks Association stated in its annual report.
-Israeli forces arrest 25 people among them three women in south Lebanon's occupied zone.
-The owner and director of a weekly magazine was sentenced to 60 days in jail for slandering Saudi Arabia's King Fahd.
